description: Goal artifact — a time-boxed outcome target with measurable key results. Stored per-goal in state/goals/<id>.yaml (whole-document YAML frontmatter is the whole file — no prose markdown body). Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-06-deliverable-rollup-render-and-fk-population.md § C1. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-13-close-weekly-goal-loop.md § C1 (.md→.yaml migration, reverses the above's format decision)
_additionalProperties_note: Permissive by design — additionalProperties is not set to false here, consistent with the handoff schema. A misspelled field will silently pass. This is intentional for forward-compatibility and matches the existing permissive pattern in other coordinator schemas. TOP-LEVEL posture reconfirmed 2026-07-25 (goal-kr-field-ownership-convention, C2): tightening was considered and DECLINED — debt-backlog.schema.json:10 cites this schema's permissiveness by name as its own precedent, and cross-repo-commitment.schema.json:10 cites goal implicitly via its own 'matches the existing permissive pattern in other coordinator schemas' clause (it names 'handoff' explicitly but not 'goal' by name — goal is one of those 'other coordinator schemas' it means, so a tightening here would still strand that citation even though the word 'goal' isn't present at cross-repo-commitment.schema.json:10 for a future reader to find directly). Unlike skill.schema.json:7 (which cleared a documented zero-out-of-set-keys corpus bar across 32 observed files before going strict), no equivalent corpus proof exists for goal records. By contrast, key_results.items.properties.reassessment_proposal (added in the same change) IS strict (additionalProperties: false + required) — it is a greenfield object with no sibling-schema citation to strand and no corpus to clear, so none of the grounds above apply to it; the top-level decline and the nested strictness are deliberately asymmetric, not in tension.

schema.description: Schema discriminator — always 'goal'. Enables kind-first schema matching.

id.description: Stable canonical goal identifier (e.g. 'goal-shipping-velocity'). Kebab-case; unique across the repo. Used as the FK value in artifact frontmatter goal: fields.

title.description: Business-legible display name for this goal.

status.description: Goal lifecycle status. active=in flight; achieved=key results met; abandoned=cancelled or superseded.

objective.description: Prose statement of what this goal aims to achieve. Written as a complete sentence. This is the 'O' in OKR.

key_results.description: Ordered list of measurable key results for this goal (the 'KR' in OKR). Each item is a concrete, falsifiable result. An empty array is permitted — a goal may be authored before KRs are defined (inception phase). No cross-field rule requires at least one KR for status:active; the assumption is that KRs are added before a goal is acted on.

id.description: Stable identifier for this key result within the goal (e.g. 'kr-1', 'kr-throughput'). Stable across edits so FK references survive reordering.

text.description: Human-readable description of the key result. Written as a measurable outcome.

kind.description: output=a deliverable/artifact produced; outcome=a measurable change in behaviour or state.

status.description: Current progress on this key result. not-started=no work begun; in-progress=active; met=achieved; at-risk=blocked or behind.

weekly_perceptible.description: True if progress on this key result should be visible in a weekly changelog or status report.

evidence_source.description: Path or reference to the artifact, metric, or document that evidences completion. Null when not yet known.

proposed_status.description: The status reassess-goal-krs proposes for this KR — NOT yet written to the live status field above. Same value space as status; distinguishing this from status IS the point (goals-okr-system.md § Weekly KR re-assessment: 'writes the proposed status back to the artifact for EM/PM confirmation — not a silent auto-set').

perceptible_movement.description: Whether reassess-goal-krs judged this KR to have moved perceptibly since the prior reassessment — the signal the wiki's re-assessment section describes alongside the proposed status.

proposed_at.description: Date the proposal was written (YYYY-MM-DD) — provenance for when, paired with proposed_by for by-what.

proposed_by.description: Actor that authored this proposal (e.g. 'reassess-goal-krs') — provenance for by-what, paired with proposed_at for when.

reassessment_proposal.description: Pending KR-status reassessment proposal awaiting EM/PM confirmation, or null when there is none outstanding. Confirmation is out-of-band: an EM/PM that accepts the proposal writes proposed_status into the live status field above and clears this back to null — this field itself is never read as the live status. Strict object shape (additionalProperties: false + required) — a typo'd key or a proposal missing one of its four subfields fails validation rather than passing silently. Not listed in key_results.items.required: most KRs carry no outstanding proposal.

owner.description: EM or workstream identifier owning this goal. Optional — may be unassigned at inception.

period.description: Time horizon this goal operates over. day=sprint/daily; week=weekly cadence; repo=workstream-scoped; quarter=quarterly OKR (e.g. Q3-2026); year=annual OKR. Required — no null branch (the Director of Engineering F2/D-C): emit-goal-from-artifact.py hard-requires period at emission time (SKIPs + _EMIT_FAIL=1 if absent), so a null/absent period must be rejected at authoring time, not silently SKIP'd later at emit.

period_value.description: The period's concrete value: an ISO-week (e.g. '2026-W29') when period=week, 'Q3-2026'-shaped when period=repo/quarter, an ISO-date when period=day. Required — emit-goal-from-artifact.py already hard-requires this from frontmatter (SKIPs + _EMIT_FAIL=1 if absent) and the deterministic goal_id is sha1(repo|root|period|period_value|text) (append-goal-event.py:187); making it required here closes the gap at the contract, not the emitter.

weekly_perceptible.description: TOP-LEVEL goal-scope weekly-perceptibility flag, distinct from the existing per-KR key_results[].weekly_perceptible — cockpit's weekly/CEO view. Optional. Wire projection is 1:1 passthrough (no OR-over-KRs derivation — see C11's field map).

parent_goal_id.description: Weekly goal → parent quarter/repo OKR linkage. Schema'd annotation only in this plan (DEC-2) — not made queryable here. Optional; null when this goal has no parent OKR.

initiative.description: Goal-side reverse FK to the initiative entity (state/initiatives/<id>.yaml) — lets a goal name the initiative it serves without scanning every initiative's goals[] array. Additive companion to the authoritative forward edge initiative.goals[] (many-to-many); this reverse edge is a single-value soft tag with no referential enforcement, fleet-consistent with the initiative: FK on handoff/plan/roadmap (D9 present-as-null, never .optional(); non-empty string when non-null). On conflict between this field and initiative.goals[], the forward array is authoritative for cockpit's buildLadder render. Spec backlink: cross-repo/inbox/2026-07-13-claude-klabauter-em-goal-side-initiative-reverse-fk-additive.md

goal_id.description: Deterministic content-derived authoring identifier: sha1(repo|root|period|period_value|text), computable at author time. This IS the C15 structured-records facet key (the SQLite facet index dedup key) — it is INTENTIONALLY DISTINCT from the wire goal_id, which append-goal-event.py derives independently from an emitter-constructed, id-prefixed text (`"<id>: <objective>"`, not the bare text/objective this field hashes). `--goal-id` is accepted by append-goal-event.py but not substituted for the wire goal_id (out of scope for C11 — see plan body); the two goal_id values are expected to diverge, not to match. Distinct from the stable canonical `id` field (project-rag excludes id/name from metadata promotion as a chunk-id-slot collision; goal_id is unambiguously non-colliding).

deliverable_id.description: The durable deliverable join key, minted once at the earliest artifact and carried verbatim by every downstream artifact; null or absent when this record predates the spine. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-08-08-sizing-objects-join-the-deliverable-spine.md § C9.
